chunks: And it is narrated from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, who said:
The mudabbar is from the one-third, and a man has the right to retract regarding his one-third, whether he made a bequest in health or illness.

key_terms.أَوْصَى: He made a bequest or will
key_terms.الثُّلُثِ: The one-third portion of the estate available for bequest
key_terms.الْمُدَبَّرُ: A slave whose emancipation is tied to the owner's death
key_terms.يَرْجِعَ: To retract or revoke the bequest

ai.seo_question: Is a mudabbar counted from one-third of the estate, and can the bequest be revoked?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that a mudabbar is counted within the one-third of the estate disposed of by bequest. It also states that a man may retract his bequest concerning that one-third, whether the bequest was made during health or during illness.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3461 - It is narrated from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (as), peace be upon them, who said:

"A mudabbar (a slave promised freedom after the owner's death) is considered to be from the one-third (of the estate). A man has the right to retract from his bequest regarding this one-third, whether he made the will during his health or illness."
